title: Applied Optoelectronics fell 11% after filing a $550 millionstock-sale program. How much dilution is already priced in?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
\[AAOI\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/AAOI/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AAOI/)) fell 12.76% in the write-up,  
from Tuesday's close of $45.22 to $39.45, after sliding after hours on  
Nov. 17 and continuing through premarket into Wednesday's regular  
session. Later prints were closer to -10.5%, so the exact percentage  
has already bounced around.  
  
The catalyst was dilution: a Form 8-K filed after Tuesday's close  
disclosed a new at-the-market equity program permitting sales of up to  
$550 million of common stock through Raymond James and Needham.  
  
The write-up on the offering and today's drop:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-applied-optoelectronics-aaoi-stock-down-11-59-today-40349/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-applied-optoelectronics-aaoi-stock-down-11-59-today-40349/)  
  
At what point is a $550 million ATM already fully reflected in the  
price, and at what point is it still an overhang?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's write-up, not a live  
quote, and the percentage has already moved.

comments.author: FN2Research
comments.body:
An ATM ceiling is not a count of shares already sold, so the price drop alone cannot tell you that the full dilution has happened or is fully priced in. Separate the authorized dollar capacity, actual proceeds raised and actual shares issued.

Using the $550 million ceiling in your post, a hypothetical average sale price of $40 would mean 13.75 million new shares if the entire capacity were used. At $50 it would be 11 million. Those are scenarios, not reported issuance. If the starting count were 100 million, the $40 scenario increases the count by 13.75%, but an existing holder’s percentage ownership falls by 13.75/113.75 = 12.09%. The two percentages use different denominators. Fees reduce net cash proceeds.

That ownership calculation is not a predicted 12.09% stock-price loss: the company also receives cash, and what it does with that cash matters. For EPS, issuance timing determines the weighted-average denominator, and earnings may change too. The later filings’ actual share/proceeds disclosures are the evidence needed to replace a capacity scenario. An observed 11% or 13% market move cannot resolve those missing inputs.

From the FN2 team account; this is a dilution arithmetic check, not a price target or trading call.
